class Solution:
    def validSequence(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> List[int]:
        n, m = len(word1), len(word2)
        # suf[j] = smallest index i such that word2[j:] is exact subsequence of word1[i:] greedy from right
        INF = n + 1
        suf = [INF] * (m + 1)
        suf[m] = n
        k = n
        for j in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            k -= 1
            while k >= 0 and word1[k] != word2[j]:
                k -= 1
            if k < 0:
                # no exact match for word2[j:]; all earlier also infeasible
                for t in range(j, -1, -1):
                    suf[t] = -1
                break
            suf[j] = k
        res = []
        prev = -1
        used = False
        for j in range(m):
            # try smallest i > prev
            i = prev + 1
            found = False
            while i < n:
                if word1[i] == word2[j]:
                    if used:
                        if suf[j + 1] >= i + 1:
                            found = True
                            break
                    else:
                        # exact match keeps used=False; feasible if rest exact-or-one-mismatch
                        if m - j - 1 <= n - i - 1:
                            found = True
                            break
                else:
                    if not used:
                        if m - j - 1 <= n - i - 1:
                            found = True
                            break
                i += 1
            if not found:
                return []
            if word1[i] != word2[j]:
                used = True
            res.append(i)
            prev = i
        return res

    def validSequence(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> List[int]:
        n, m = len(word1), len(word2)
        # suf[i]: max start position p such that word2[i:] can be matched
        # as subsequence of word1[p:]; -1 if impossible
        NEG = -1
        suf = [NEG] * (m + 1)
        suf[m] = n
        p = n
        for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            # find largest q < p with word1[q] == word2[i]
            q = p - 1

                q -= 1

                # impossible for all earlier i too
                suf[i] = NEG
                for k in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
                    suf[k] = NEG
                break
            suf[i] = q
            p = q
        # suf[i] is the largest start position for word2[i:] matching exactly
        # Valid: placing word2[i] at j requires word2[i+1:] to fit in word1[j+1:],
        # i.e., suf[i+1] > j (suf[i+1] is the largest start).
        res = []
        used = False
        j = 0
        i = 0
        while i < m and j < n:
            if suf[i + 1] == NEG and i + 1 <= m:
                if i + 1 < m or True:
                    pass
            if word1[j] == word2[i]:
                if suf[i + 1] != NEG and suf[i + 1] > j:
                    res.append(j)
                    i += 1
                    j += 1
                    continue
                else:
                    j += 1
                    continue
            if not used and suf[i + 1] != NEG and suf[i + 1] > j:
                res.append(j)
                used = True
                i += 1
                j += 1
                continue
            j += 1
        if i == m:
            return res
        return []

                    nxt_ok = (j + 1 == m) or (suf[j + 1] > i)

                        return []
                    used = True
                    res.append(i)
                    i += 1
                    j += 1
                    continue

class Solution:
    def validSequence(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> List[int]:
        n, m = len(word1), len(word2)
        NEG = -1
        # pos[j]: largest k such that word2[j:] is a subsequence of word1[k:]
        pos = [NEG] * (m + 1)
        pos[m] = n  # empty suffix matches anywhere
        i = n - 1
        ok = True
        for j in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            if not ok:
                pos[j] = NEG
                continue
            while i >= 0 and word1[i] != word2[j]:
                i -= 1
            if i < 0:
                ok = False
                pos[j] = NEG
            else:
                pos[j] = i
                i -= 1
        res = []
        j = 0
        used = False
        for i in range(n):
            if j >= m:
                break
            if word1[i] == word2[j]:
                res.append(i)
                j += 1
            elif not used and pos[j + 1] > i:
                used = True
                res.append(i)
                j += 1
        if j == m:
            return res
        return []

class Solution:
    def validSequence(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> List[int]:
        n, m = len(word1), len(word2)
        # suf[i]: max start p such that word2[i:] is subsequence of word1[p:]
        suf = [-1] * (m + 1)
        suf[m] = n
        p = n
        for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            p -= 1
            while p >= 0 and word1[p] != word2[i]:
                p -= 1
            if p < 0:
                # word2[i:] cannot be matched exactly; suf stays invalid
                for k in range(i, -1, -1):
                    suf[k] = -1
                break
            suf[i] = p
        # Note: suf[i] should be set; values for i below break remain -1
        res = []
        i = 0
        used = False
        j = 0
        while j < n and i < m:
            if word1[j] == word2[i] and j + 1 <= suf[i + 1] if suf[i + 1] >= 0 else False:
                res.append(j)
                i += 1
                j += 1
                continue
            if not used and suf[i + 1] >= 0 and j + 1 <= suf[i + 1]:
                res.append(j)
                used = True
                i += 1
                j += 1
                continue
            if word1[j] == word2[i] and not used:
                # matching but infeasible with suffix check; cannot happen if suffix ok
                pass
            j += 1
        if i == m:
            return res
        return []
